editor_note: The dominant thread today is that AI is moving from experimental to operational — and every column in the budget is starting to feel the pressure. Anthropic's Code w/ Claude event signals the frontier labs are no longer just shipping models; they're building developer platforms that replace entire toolchains. Simon Willison's live dispatch confirms the convergence he'd been warning about: vibe coding and agentic engineering are becoming the same thing. Meanwhile, the Microsoft-OpenAI AGI clause quietly died — the most consequential clause in the enterprise AI ecosystem just disappeared without a press release, and that matters for every CIO modelling long-term vendor dependency. On the governance front, the UK AI Security Institute's GPT-5.5 cyber evaluation is the kind of named, dated assessment that belongs in your risk register. Match Group's hiring freeze frames the real CFO conversation: AI tools cost money, so people won't. And Altara's R&D data unification play is the narrow end of a wedge aimed squarely at pharma IT: your data siloes are the next target.
